To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the performance of a multi-relational factorization model can be improved by using target specific parameter settings and (2) a model with target specific parameters can be trained in a single run, which is efficient and scalable.

(1) optimizing the model for each target relation independently leads to a performance improvement compared to a single model optimized for a compromise over all relations; (2) the performance improvement can be obtained by using target-specific parameters, but without learning these parameters independently; and (3) the target-specific parameters can be coupled through a set of regularizing auxiliary parameters.

(1) multi-matrix factorization methods can be improved by optimizing each target relation individually, (2) the improvement is more important for target relations that are more dissimilar from each other and (3) the performance improvement comes from a more effective use of the available data.

optimizing multi-matrix factorization methods for multiple target relations, and we show that it can be achieved by using target specific but coupled parameters, which can be learned efficiently.

The main takeaway from our work is that
, for a given multi-relational learning problem, the performance of a factorization model can be significantly improved by using target-specific parameters.
, when learning a multi-matrix factorization model for a multi-target problem, it is better to optimize the model for each target separately rather than for a compromise over all of them.

, for multi-relational data, a model that is optimized for one target relation can have a better predictive performance on that relation than a model optimized for all target relations simultaneously.
